D018-D019_h001.question:
I’ve been having these flashbacks—really vivid, like I’m back there. Out of nowhere, I’ll remember the crash: the headlights, the sound of metal twisting. I can’t shut it out. Some mornings I wake up drenched in sweat, heart pounding, not sure where I am. It’s been happening since the accident—though I honestly couldn’t tell you if it’s been weeks or months. Time’s been a blur.  

Driving used to be my thing—kept me independent, you know? Now I don’t even care if I pick up fares. I used to take pride in my work, staying sharp, saving up. Not anymore. What’s the point?  

And it wasn’t my fault—that truck ran the light. They should’ve been paying attention. I keep seeing it, hearing the horn, then—*snap*—I’m flinching, sometimes jerking the wheel. Loud noises wreck me. A backfire, a siren—I jump like I’ve been shocked. My head feels thick, like I’m moving through water. Can’t focus long enough to plan my route. Fear’s just… always there. Low. Constant. Like something bad’s about to happen again.  

I just want to feel normal behind the wheel. But I don’t even know what normal is right now.

I’ve been having these flashes—out of nowhere—of that night. It’s like I’m back there, hearing the screams, feeling the adrenaline. I can’t control when they come, and they just… hijack my thoughts. At work, I’ll be writing a campaign, and suddenly I’m frozen, picturing everything in detail. It’s terrifying. The fear doesn’t go away—it’s like it’s stuck inside me, raw and constant.  

I used to call my mom every Sunday. Now, I don’t feel anything when I see her texts. My best friend tried to hug me last week, and it was like my body shut down. I don’t know how to feel love lately. It’s not that I don’t care—I just can’t *reach* it.  

And the anger… it’s new. I snapped at a colleague who bumped my coffee, threw it across the room. Shattered the mug. Last weekend I punched a wall during an argument. I didn’t even realize how tense I’ve been until I noticed my hands are always clenched.  

I don’t know when it started exactly—sometime after that night. A few weeks? Maybe less. It feels like both forever and no time at all. I can’t tell if I’m falling apart or just… adjusting.

    B. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D019_h022.question:
I’ve been having these awful dreams—reliving that night over and over, the sound, the fear, like I’m right back there. I wake up soaked in sweat, heart racing, and it takes forever to calm down. During the day, I feel on edge all the time, like something’s about to go wrong, even when nothing is. I can’t relax, not even at home. My clients notice—I snapped at one last week for no reason, raised my voice, said things I didn’t mean. I’ve never been that way before.  

It’s hard to feel good about anything lately. I closed a big policy last month—the kind I used to celebrate—but I didn’t feel a thing. No pride, no joy. My daughter even said, “Mom, why don’t you ever smile anymore?” And I want to, I really do. But it’s like a switch flipped inside me.  

I can’t tell you exactly how long this’s been going on. A few weeks? Maybe close to a month. Time blurs. I know it started after everything happened, but I haven’t kept track. I just know I’m not myself. I’m scared, irritable, and empty all at once—and I don’t know how to stop it.

D018-D019_h023.question:
I’ve been off-kilter since it happened. It was a few weeks ago—could be less, could be a bit more, I don’t even track the days now. I was picking up a fare near the highway when I saw the crash—two cars, head-on. I couldn’t stop in time to look away. One of the drivers looked right at me, eyes wide, just before… well, you know. Since then, I keep seeing it. Not like a memory—it’s sharper. I’ll be sitting at a red light, and suddenly I’m back there: the glass shattering, the scream. I’ll snap out of it gripping the wheel, heart pounding, not knowing how much time passed.

I can’t talk to anyone about it. My ex asked, but I shut down. Not out of anger—at least, not then. It’s like I’m hollow. Nothing touches me. No joy, no real sadness. Just numb. But then little things set me off—somebody cuts me off, says the wrong thing, and I explode. Cursing, shouting, not even caring who hears. Afterward? Nothing again. Like I wasn’t even there. I feel… ashamed, I guess. Not sure why, but like I should’ve done something that day. I don’t know how long this’ll last. I just want it to stop.

D018-D019_h024.question:
I’ve been having these flashes—moments when I’m right back there, like I’m reliving it. It’s not just a memory; it hits me in my chest, in my hands, like I can feel it again. I don’t want to, but it just crashes in—no warning. Sometimes it’s a sound, other times nothing at all. I work with wood, build custom pieces—used to love the quiet rhythm of sanding, the smell of finish on cloth. Now I’ll be in the middle of a cut and suddenly I’m not in the shop anymore.  

I feel… small, like I’ve done something wrong, even though I know I didn’t. It’s a weight, especially when someone’s kind to me or something goes right—I just shut down. Joy feels like something that belongs to someone else. I used to laugh with my daughter. Now I just watch her like she’s on the other side of glass.  

And my nerves—I’m raw. A coworker bumped a tool the other day, metal clanged, and I snapped at him so hard he stepped back. I didn’t mean to. Everything feels like it’s too much—too loud, too close, too fast. I can’t tell if this started weeks ago or a few months. Time’s been… off. I just know I’m not me anymore.

D018-D019_h025.question:
I’ve been having these dreams—over and over—about *that night*. I don’t like talking about it, but yeah, it was bad. In the dream, I’m right back there, heart pounding, can’t move, and I wake up soaked in sweat like I just finished a set of heavy lifts. It’s not just once in a while—it’s frequent, and it’s messing with my sleep.  

Since then, I feel… wired all the time. Like, even in the gym—my own space, where I’m supposed to be in control—I get this sudden rage if someone touches my equipment or cuts in line. One time I snapped at a regular member over nothing. Felt terrible after, but in the moment, I couldn’t stop it.  

I used to love coaching clients, seeing them hit milestones. Now, even when someone nails a PR, I don’t feel anything. I smile, I nod, but inside it’s empty. Pride? Satisfaction? Can’t tap into that anymore.  

I don’t know *when* it started exactly—sometime after—well, after what happened. Could’ve been weeks ago. I’m not sleeping, I’m on edge, but is it long enough to matter? I don’t know. I just know I don’t feel like myself.
